data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $450M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $450M total raised as a proxy base, implying $900M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B reflecting the heterogeneity of nuclear venture funding.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $687M (low) to $1.0B (high), with a median of $854M. The $213M spread between low and high estimates reflects divergence between stage-progression methodology and peer-median anchoring, as well as the wide dispersion within the nuclear energy peer set itself. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to near-term peers and the degree to which later-stage funding multiples in this sector apply to a Series A-stage asset.
